answer: Each identity posts a 60-credit bond and keeps one tide of work in pipeline escrow: tide T pays only after the next tide's item is escrowed. The item is sealed with an owner-key cipher, blocking cross-clone copies. A hollow slot earns nothing and loses 20 after one tide. Auditors recompute the public queue; duplicates burn both bonds. Fees start at 20, rising 5 per further block of 100, so the 1000th pays 65; 1,000 fakes lock 60,000 and pay 42,500 in fees. Rented items fail: they carry the seller's key, so the cipher seal mismatches. An honest identity pays 20 once and is paid one tide later.
